title: ALT-dominance adds no transferable fasting-insulin prediction beyond flexible enzyme and metabolic measures in two NHANES cohorts
abstract: A literature-led enzyme-balance feature, max(log(ALT/AST),0), was added to a ridge spline model of standard metabolic measures and individual liver enzymes. Models were trained in1900 eligible NHANES2007–2008 adults and frozen for2171 different NHANES2009–2010 adults. Fasting-weighted log-insulin MSE changed from0.241875 to0.242927; baseline-minus-augmented gain was-0.001052 (500 source-refit/target-resample rescaled PSU bootstrap95% interval -0.003371 to0.000302). A small source cross-validation improvement did not transfer. Regularization, linear-baseline, sex and enzyme-exclusion checks retained negative target point estimates. This is a negative test of incremental representation, not evidence against enzyme–insulin associations generally. Separate survey cycles establish participant-cohort transfer testing, not geographic or platform generalization; insulin is not clamp-measured resistance.
